newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's trade deficit with China jumps in March.
newsitem.headline: Japan's trade deficit with China jumps in March.

text.p: Japan's trade deficit with China more than quadrupled in March from a year earlier, backed by an abundant inflow of clothing imports, and economists said the trend was likely to continue due to China's cheap labour costs.
Tokyo posted a deficit of 190.94 billion yen ($1.51 billion) with China in March, a rise of 335.9 percent from a year earlier, according to Finance Ministry data released on Thursday.
A ministry official said imports of clothing and related goods were the main factors behind the deficit.
But he played down the magnitude of the jump, saying the deficit itself had been at more or less the same level recently.
In February, Japan's trade deficit with Beijing was 179.79 billion yen ($1.42 billion), while in January it stood at 292.13 billion yen ($2.31 billion), the official said.
The deficit with China stood out amid the overall trade account which showed a surplus of 818.34 billion yen ($6.49 billion) in March.
The deficit with China more than offsets Japan's surplus with all of the European Union nations, which stood at 131.29 billion yen ($1.04 billion) in March.
The Finance Ministry official said it was difficult to forecast the trade account outlook with China due to various factors, such as future exchange rates and the economic conditions of both nations.
But economists said imports of labour-intensive products such as clothing from China were unlikely to slow down soon.

"From the late 1980s, imports from China of products like clothing which require a large labour force with cheap wages have increased," said Tomoo Marukawa, an economist at the Institute of Developing Economies in Tokyo.
He added that many Japanese clothing firms have moved their production centres to China and that this was also contributing to the flow of imported clothing into Japan.
Marukawa said Japanese firms were likely to increase production in China.
"Some people say that by the year 2000, half of the clothes worn by the Japanese will be made in China," he said.
Unlike its trade surplus with the United States, often a source of friction between the two nations, the huge imbalance with China has so far not come into the spotlight.
Although the Japanese government has in the past complained of dumping by the Chinese of textiles, it has voiced little concern about the recent trade deficit with Beijing.
"We don't evaluate the conditions of our trade account with every individual nation. I'm not in a position to comment whether Japan is 'concerned' or not," said the finance ministry official.
